matches.summary: Lost 2–3 to a side from the division above. Out-shot 22 to 11 with 35% possession, but Karlsen and Frederiksen scored. 825 at Kløvermarken.
Won 1–0 at Boresko Park. A long ball, Andersen's knock-down and Noah Jakobsen rifled it home in the 91st minute. Sundby edged it on shots (12–7) and xG (1.29–0.41).
2–0 up after three minutes, 3–5 down at the end. Hellerup, from the division above, had 71% of the ball and scored five times from 11 shots on target.
Pyne-Cole scored after two minutes from Andersen's pass, then Magnus Schou scored twice either side of half-time. Næsby out-shot Sundby 19–10 (xG 2.71–0.73).
4–0 up by half-time. 20 shots to 7, xG 2.77 to 0.36. Noah Jakobsen scored one and set up two.
First league win, and a Belmaillah hat-trick (9.97): the hoof chase, a penalty and a curler. Lind's 91st-minute goal was a consolation. Up to 6th.
Paludan scored twice before half-time. Noah Jakobsen came on and pulled one back straight after the break, but Vanløse had 16 shots to 6 (xG 2.27–0.44). Down to 8th.
Frouland scored after 7 minutes and Djafer-Bey added a second in first-half stoppage time. Bastian Andersen's 87th-minute goal came too late. Frem had 11 shots to 6. Down to 10th.
0–0 after 90 minutes. In extra time, Mølvadgaard curled a free kick over the wall in the 112th minute. A first clean sheet, with the new back four.
Expected to lose, won 3–0. Mølvadgaard opened the scoring, Pyne-Cole added two, and Elliott Karlsen set up two (8.6). Second clean sheet in a row. Up to 8th.
Absorbed 60% possession, then struck late: Andersen chipped the keeper after an error, then Belmaillah finished in the 90th. Seven shots on target to three. Third clean sheet in a row. Up to 5th.
Beat the league leaders 1–0. Andersen set up Belmaillah on 36 minutes. The only clear-cut chance of the game was Sundby's. Fourth clean sheet in a row. Up to 2nd.

Giant-killing: beat Superliga AC Horsens, three divisions above. Horsens had 75% of the ball, but Mølvadgaard came off the bench and headed in from close range on 84 minutes. Player of the match (7.9).

Rotated side lost 2–0. Damsgaard conceded a penalty, Tønnesen scored it (25'), and Bøgedal added a second in first-half stoppage time. Went very attacking after the break: 12 shots, but chances worth only 0.85 goals.

Beat 2nd-placed Brønshøj with 28% of the ball. Belmaillah scored after 18 minutes, then Pyne-Cole volleyed in Mølvadgaard's low cross in the 90th. More clear-cut chances (2–1) and more expected goals (1.37–1.15). Up to 2nd.
Deserved win over Johansen's new club. Graini curled in from 19 metres, Mølvadgaard finished low into the corner, and Becker's own goal made it nervy. 12 shots to 5, 7 on target to 1.
Top-of-the-table clash lost to Kisum's 18th-minute free kick. Sundby managed one shot all game, none on target. FC Helsingør go top.
0–0 away at Næsby, the side who led the league for most of the season. A first clean sheet against a top side, but a second game in a row without a goal. Rasmus Fink made his debut off the bench.
Back to winning ways in a gale. Mølvadgaard drove in from 19 metres on 49 minutes. 21 shots and 3 clear-cut chances, but only one goal. Up to 3rd.
Cup run ends. FC Fredericia had 73% of the ball and William Madsen (8.5) scored twice from defensive midfield: a volley into the top corner, then a skidding drive after a Langhorn error.
Tired after the midweek cup tie and lucky to get a point. Holbæk had 70% of the ball and twice the expected goals. Jakobsen scored after a defensive error; Stolshøj equalised on 74 minutes.
Heartbreak at the leaders. An even game (12 shots to 13, xG 1.05 to 1.18) until the 92nd minute, when Kunnerup lost the ball and Frem broke for Kretzschmar to score.
A 1–1 at Hørsholm-Usserød. Belmaillah scored just before half-time, after another goal had been wrongly disallowed. Hvid headed the equaliser on 59 minutes.

story.label: Week 20 · 7–13 November
story.title: Week 20: Heartbreak in stoppage time
story.body:
Away at leaders Frem, on a gusty, drizzly afternoon at the Valby Stadion in front of 788. Frem had 61% of the ball, but most of it ended in long-range efforts. It was as even as top-of-the-table games get: 12 shots to 13, five on target each, and xG of 1.05 to 1.18. Vandal was Sundby's best at 7.0. Karsberg, Frem's player of the match (7.7), was the threat all afternoon.

Then, two minutes into stoppage time, Kunnerup gave the ball away. Frem broke, Karsberg crossed, and Kretzschmar volleyed in from close range. 1–0. The local paper called Sundby "surprisingly lacklustre". One fan's verdict: "Nothing worse than conceding a late winner."

It was Frem's sixth win in a row. Elsewhere, Helsingør lost 2–0 at Hørsholm-Usserød, so the gap to 2nd is still four points. Sundby stay 3rd on 23, seven behind Frem, with Næsby and ASA a point behind on 22. Belmaillah, without a goal for a while, has publicly vowed to end his drought.

Next: Hørsholm-Usserød away, the last game before the winter break. The league returns on 6 March against Holstebro.

story.label: Week 19 · 1–7 November
story.title: Week 19: Tired legs, lucky point
story.body:
Three days after the cup exit, a weary Sundby hosted Holbæk. It showed: Holbæk had 70% of the ball, 11 corners to 2, and twice the expected goals.

Noah Jakobsen put Sundby ahead on 57 minutes after a Holbæk error, set up by right-back Noah Schak, who was player of the match (7.5). Stolshøj equalised on 74 minutes, set up by ex-Sundby man Matin Al-Atlassi. 1–1, and Sundby were glad of it.

The cost: Jakobsen picked up an injury, and there's a fitness worry over Jørgensen.

Next: Frem, second in the table.

story.label: Week 18 · 26 October–1 November
story.title: Week 18: The cup run ends with honour
story.body:
The Danish Cup fourth round brought FC Fredericia, a much bigger club, to Kløvermarken. Sundby held them for 54 minutes. Then William Madsen, a defensive midfielder, volleyed into the top corner. On 76 minutes a Langhorn error let him in for a second.

Fredericia had 73% of the ball and the better chances, but it was never a thrashing. Graini was Sundby's best player again (7.1). Bassett threw on Belmaillah, Mølvadgaard, Trkulja, Elliott Karlsen and Frederiksen, but the subs couldn't find a way back.

A noble defeat. Three cup wins, a Superliga scalp, and now full focus on the league.

story.label: Week 17 · 19–25 October
story.title: Week 17: Mølvadgaard ends the drought
story.body:
The slide shows in the table: Sundby are 4th, five points behind leaders FC Helsingør, and have lost three of their last five home league games. Two games without a goal.

Next up is bottom-of-the-table Ringsted at Kløvermarken: 7 points from 12 games, one away win in five. The pundits make Sundby favourites, but only just: 49% for a win, 26% a draw, 25% for Ringsted. Sundby beat them 3–1 in August with Belmaillah's hat-trick.

A gale is forecast. Need a win.

They got it. Bassett picked his goal-scorers: Mølvadgaard and Pyne-Cole up front, with Fink making his first start on the right. Four minutes after half-time, Mølvadgaard drove one in from 19 metres. 1–0.

It should have been more: 21 shots, 3 clear-cut chances and 2.05 expected goals. But after two blanks, nobody minded. Mølvadgaard was player of the match (8.6), his sixth goal of the season and every one of them has mattered. Another clean sheet.

Sundby climb back to 3rd, three points behind FC Helsingør.

story.label: Week 16 · 12–18 October
story.title: Week 16: Honours even, still no goals
story.body:
Næsby away, the team that led the league for most of the season. Sundby held them to 0–0 at the ALPI Arena: another clean sheet against a top side, but a second game in a row without a goal.

The brightest moment came off the bench. Rasmus Fink, who complained weeks ago about not playing, finally made his debut on 79 minutes. The fans loved it: "Our fans won't shut up about Fink now."

The papers are worried about Bastian Andersen's goal drought.

Next: Ringsted, bottom of the table.

story.label: Week 15 · 5–11 October
story.title: Week 15: One shot, no goals, no top spot
story.body:
Second against third, with a chance to go top. FC Helsingør took it instead.

Mathias Kisum curled a free kick into the top corner after 18 minutes, and Sundby never replied. One shot all afternoon, none on target, expected goals of 0.02. The low block held, but there was nothing behind it.

The fans noticed: "We have got absolutely no creativity in this side whatsoever."

Off the pitch, captain Becker reports that Andreas Nybro is unhappy about his lack of games.

FC Helsingør go top. Next: leaders-turned-chasers Næsby.

story.label: Week 14 · 28 September–4 October
story.title: Week 14: Promise broken, ASA brushed aside
story.body:
Saturday morning, two hours before kick-off: Benjamin Juel-Berg complained that Bassett hadn't kept his promise about playing time. By 11:30 he'd been released on a free. That's the fourth senior player Bassett has let go.

Then ASA, Aarhus, Johansen's new club, came to Kløvermarken. Noah Graini curled one in from 19 metres, Mølvadgaard finished low into the corner, and only a Becker own goal made it close. Sundby had 12 shots to 5 and 7 on target to 1. Graini was player of the match (7.9).

Sundby stay 2nd, a point behind Næsby, who lost at FC Helsingør. Helsingør are next.

story.label: Week 13 · 21–27 September
story.title: Week 13: Wasps stung
story.body:
Brønshøj, second in the table, at the Tingbjerg Ground. They had 72% of the ball. Sundby won 2–0.

Belmaillah scored after 18 minutes. Then Sundby sat in, Poulsen made save after save (player of the match, 7.6), and in the 90th minute Mølvadgaard crossed low and hard from the right for Pyne-Cole to volley in.

The papers are "still wondering" how Sundby won. The numbers say they deserved it: two clear-cut chances to one, and more expected goals despite barely touching the ball.

Sundby go back up to 2nd, level on points with FC Helsingør and four behind Næsby.

Next: ASA, Aarhus, Johansen's new club.

story.label: Week 12 · 14–20 September
story.title: Week 12: Giant-killing, then a reality check
story.body:
Danish Cup third round, and a giant at Kløvermarken: AC Horsens of the Superliga, three divisions above Sundby. They had 75% of the ball. Sundby barely touched it but kept them out.

On came Damsgaard for his debut and Mølvadgaard for the last 20 minutes. On 84 minutes Trkulja broke down the left, the long ball went forward, and Mølvadgaard got to it first and headed in from close range. 1–0.

His second cup winner off the bench in three weeks, and player of the match (7.9). The papers called it a smash and grab and a damp squib. 87 people saw it. Nobody at Sundby cares.

The same day, Marius Hausted was released on a free. Damsgaard had signed the day before. The third senior player gone in three weeks.

Six wins in a row. Five clean sheets in a row. Amateurs from the third tier have knocked a Superliga club out of the cup.

Three days later, a reality check. With fitness a worry, Bassett rested four players and handed debuts in both full-back spots to Schak and Damsgaard. Inside 25 minutes Damsgaard gave away a penalty, Tønnesen scored it, and Bøgedal added a second just before half-time.

The half-time hairdryer fired most of them up, and Sundby went very attacking. Twelve shots, but nothing clear-cut. Holstebro 2–0 Sundby.

The run ends at six wins. Sundby stay 3rd, two points behind Brønshøj, who come to Kløvermarken next. One fan summed it up: "Haven't seen finishing that wasteful in a very long time."

story.label: Week 11 · 7–13 September
story.title: Week 11: Top of the league, beaten
story.body:
Hørsholm-Usserød came to Kløvermarken top of the table. They left beaten.

The big man and the fast man: on 36 minutes Bastian Andersen set up Belmaillah, and that was enough. Hørsholm had 60% of the ball and eight shots but no clear-cut chances. Sundby had the only one, and scored it: a deft close-range finish. Andersen was player of the match (7.5).

It wasn't pretty. Hørsholm fouled their way through it, and one fan wished luck to anyone making a highlights package "from that dross". Only 88 people were there to see it.

Four clean sheets in a row. Five wins in a row. And a month after being 10th, Sundby are 2nd, one point behind Næsby.

Next: AC Horsens in the cup.

story.label: Week 10 · 31 August–6 September
story.title: Week 10: Chat shit, get banged, then win at Ishøj
story.body:
Two days after the Holbæk win, captain Johan Becker came to Bassett with a warning: Magnus Krogh Hansen, an "influential player", was unhappy and wanted to start more games.

Bassett had a word with him. By 5pm Krogh Hansen had been released on a free transfer.

That's two senior players gone in a week: the vice-captain for defending badly, and the forward for complaining. Nobody seems bothered by the brutal regime. The September dynamics report rates the club atmosphere "very good": 19 of the 21 first-team players are very happy, and team cohesion is average but improving. The only unhappy player isn't even in the first-team squad.

The one open issue: Benjamin Juel-Berg is worried new signing Jovanovski will take his place, and seven teammates agree with him. Bassett has promised him something. With this manager, he'd better keep his head down.

Then Ishøj away, third in the table. Sundby sat deep, let them have 60% of the ball, and waited. On 76 minutes keeper Marius Kruse made a mistake and Bastian Andersen chipped him delicately. In the 90th minute Belmaillah, the poacher, rounded it off with a well-struck finish. 0–2.

A sweet one for Mølvadgaard too: Ishøj are his former club. One fan summed it up: "We were excellent today, defended as a unit and allowed the forwards to do their thing."

Three clean sheets in a row since the new back four came in, with Jørgensen the best defender on the pitch again (7.8). Bassett told them nobody gave them a chance. Most of them looked delighted.

Sundby are up to 5th, two points off the top.

story.label: Week 9 · 29 August
story.title: Week 9: Written off, three goals up
story.body:
Board and fans expected defeat at Holbæk. Sundby won 3–0.

Mølvadgaard scored again after 18 minutes, from Elliott Karlsen's pass. Pyne-Cole added two after the break, one set up by Graini, the other by Elliott Karlsen again. Elliott Karlsen was the best player on the pitch (8.6).

Second clean sheet in a row, and the first in the league. Noah Schak got the debut the fans wanted, at right-back. Holbæk had 66% of the ball and only three shots on target.

Sundby climb to 8th on six points. Goal difference is positive (+2) for the first time, and fifth place is only two points away. The papers led with Elliott Karlsen's form. Social media was split: one fan loves him, another says it's too much hype, a third asks if everyone's on the bandwagon yet.

story.label: Week 8 · 24–30 August
story.title: Week 8: Someone takes the blame, the new back four delivers
story.body:
After the data came the reckoning. Bassett ripped up the 4-2-4 for a cautious 4-4-2 with two holding midfielders: sit in a low block, drop off, and hit teams on the break.

A whole new back four: Langhorn, Jørgensen, Jovanovski and Vandal, all of them bench players last week. Sørensen and Hausted are out.

And someone had to take the blame. Vice-captain Gustav Lundqvist, the right-back with a marking score of 4, was released on a free transfer. Now Sundby need a new vice-captain.

First test: Tårnby away in the cup. A low block, a tight game, and 0–0 after 90 minutes. Then, in the 112th minute, a free kick. Mølvadgaard, signed for nothing a fortnight ago, curled it over the wall and in. Free kicks were on the training schedule every Thursday.

Tårnby 0–1 Sundby. The new back four's first game: a clean sheet. Jørgensen (7.5) and Jovanovski (7.4) were the best defenders on the pitch.

The reward: AC Horsens in the cup third round. Trialist striker Julian Vitus Pedersen also signed on a free, with four days of the transfer window left.

The table before kick-off: Sundby 10th on three points, Holbæk 11th, goal difference -5. Belmaillah is joint third in the league's scoring charts.

Next: Holbæk away, 11th against 10th. The team second from bottom are somehow favourites. Board and fans both expect Sundby to lose. That's how low confidence has sunk. The fans' only wish: a debut for Noah Schak.

story.label: Week 7 · Analysis
story.title: What the data says: easy to roll over
story.body:
The analysts' verdict after four league games: plenty of problems defensively, fairly poor in attack, "very easy to roll over."

Defence is the big one. Sundby concede almost two a game, and the chances they allow say that's deserved. Opponents have had 56 shots to Sundby's 38 and seven clear-cut chances to three. No clean sheets, about 12 fouls a game, two penalties conceded, and early goals against Vanløse (5 minutes) and Frem (7).

The 4-2-4 leaves the middle empty. Opponents have had around 60% of the ball, and Sundby rarely win it back high up. The analysts' best XI is a cautious 4-4-2 with two holding midfielders.

Up front, Sundby have scored six from chances worth about four, mostly thanks to Belmaillah's hat-trick against the bottom side. Only one cross in ten finds a teammate, and when the long ball doesn't stick there's no plan B.

Individuals: Søren Sørensen's passing is the weak link at the back. Gustav Frederiksen's tackling and heading stand out in midfield. Karlo Trkulja's physical output is off the charts.

The board? B-, Pleased. For now.

story.label: Week 7 · 17–23 August
story.title: Week 7: Frem make it three league defeats
story.body:
After last week, a must-win. Frem come to Kløvermarken in 11th, third from bottom. Around 660 tickets are expected, more than three times Sundby's average of 195, and 600 of them are Frem fans. The ground holds 1,200.

It went wrong again. Frem led after seven minutes and doubled it in first-half stoppage time. Bastian Andersen scored his first Sundby goal on 87 minutes, set up by Pyne-Cole, but it was only a consolation. 1–2.

The papers called it a deserved Frem win. Three defeats in four league games, and Sundby slip to 10th on three points, above only Holbæk on goal difference and bottom side Ringsted. They look every bit the relegation favourites they were tipped to be.

Behind the scenes, Bassett confirmed a new appointment: Paulsen joins the staff.

story.label: Week 6 · 10–16 August
story.title: Week 6: Free-transfer frenzy, then a home defeat
story.body:
Amateurs train twice a week, so every session counts. Bassett is spending Thursdays on the final third, free kicks and corners. If you can't pass through teams, you can still beat them from a dead ball.

Then a busy Saturday morning: four free signings before kick-off. Target forward Marcus Mølvadgaard, playmaker Devrim Sahin, midfielder Issah Salou (who speaks no Danish) and young centre-back Noah Schak. Cost: nothing.

Then a defeat. Vanløse's Paludan scored twice before half-time, and Noah Jakobsen came off the bench to pull one back seconds after the break. That was as close as it got: 16 shots to 6, and Sundby drop to 8th. They were shite, and Bassett told them so: "I don't like what I just saw from this team." Most of them looked inspired. Bastian Andersen just looked stressed.

Next: Frem at home.

story.label: Week 5 · 3–9 August
story.title: Week 5: Cup demolition, Belmaillah hat-trick
story.body:
Danish Cup first round at Virum-Sorgenfri, and Sundby were 4–0 up by half-time. Trkulja scored twice, Noah Jakobsen scored one and made two (8.6), and Belmaillah added the fourth. Twenty shots to seven.

Then Ringsted away in the league, with a draw expected. 0–0 at half-time, but Sundby were the better side.

After the break, Belmaillah took over. First a bizarre goal: Kunnerup hoofed it from halfway, keeper Fischer charged out, and Belmaillah got there first. Then a penalty. Then a peach, curled in from the edge of the box after Juel-Berg's pass. Hat-trick, rated 9.97.

Ringsted 1–3 Sundby. First league win, up to 6th.

Perspective: the media tip Ringsted to finish bottom. Sundby are now predicted 10th, up one place.

story.label: Pre-season · Week 4 · 27 July–2 August
story.title: Week 4: One in, one out, one up, two down
story.body:
Done deal: Simeon Jovanovski signs until 2028 on £3.3K a year. That's the entire wage budget on one 20-year-old Swede.

The bad news: right-back Alexander Johansen, who started the friendlies, walked out on a free to ASA, Aarhus, the title favourites in Sundby's own league.

League opener against Næsby, in a Route One 4-2-4 with both new centre-backs starting. It began perfectly: Bastian Andersen set up Pyne-Cole after two minutes. Then Magnus Schou scored either side of half-time and Sundby lost 1–2.

Fair result. Næsby had 19 shots to 10 and the only clear-cut chances. Poulsen (7.5) kept it close.

story.label: Pre-season · Week 3 · 20–26 July
story.title: Week 3: Five out, five conceded
story.body:
Signing number two: Andreas Nybro, 22, a 5'6" right wing-back on an amateur deal. Quick (acceleration 15), tireless (determination 15) and with the strength of a paper bag (2). He's played 47 games for five clubs.

Then the cull began. Five players were released on free transfers in a single afternoon: goalkeeper Oscar Brinkmann, Nielsen, Klein, Foss and Dal Møller. Another trialist, Mundt, is on his way in.

At BK Skjold, route one at its best: centre-back Mads Jul Jørgensen broke out of defence and Giran Pyne-Cole struck it home. Sundby 2–1 up after 73 minutes.

Then an appalling afternoon against Hellerup IK. Hausted and Pyne-Cole had Sundby 2–0 up inside three minutes. Pyne-Cole got another to make it 3–3 at half-time, but Hellerup, from the division above, took 71% of the ball and won 5–3. Some mitigation, but not much.

Next: the real thing. Næsby at home on 1 August.

story.label: Pre-season · Week 2 · 13–19 July
story.title: Week 2: Hoof, flick, bang, and a big bet
story.body:
The plan worked at the first time of asking. At Roskilde KFUM, with a 0–0 looking certain, a big hoof up the field found Bastian Andersen. He knocked it down and Noah Jakobsen rifled it home in the 91st minute. 1–0.

It wasn't a smash and grab either: Sundby had 12 shots to 7 and the only clear-cut chances. Lucas Poulsen kept a clean sheet and Jakobsen was player of the match.

The books: £5.27K in the bank and a projected £65K loss this season. So naturally Bassett is about to spend every penny of the remaining £3.4K-a-year wage budget on one player: trialist Simeon Jovanovski, a 20-year-old Swedish centre-back from Malmö FF. He was rated 7.5 at Roskilde and the staff rate him 5 stars. Worth every krone.

Also on trial: Louis Keita, a 6'8" centre-back with a jumping reach of 17 and a technique of 2. He played three games for Sundby last season. A very Bassett sort of player.

Next: BK Skjold away on Wednesday, then Hellerup IK at home.

story.label: Pre-season · Week 1 · 6–12 July
story.title: Week 1: Blank faces, brave defeat, first signing
story.body:
Dave Bassett, 42, takes charge with no badges, no caps and an 'obscure' reputation. Sundby are tipped 11th of 12. Transfer budget: zero.

His first team talk was met with blank faces. Captain Johan Becker hopes he's as convincing when it matters. The press conference drew one journalist. It could have been an email.

The plan: sit in, win it, go direct to a big man and a fast lad. Simple, because they're amateurs.

Thirteen strikers came in on trial, and seven were sent home on day one. Six remain to fight for the big-man role. Five more arrived for the left wing, including Ringsted's Mikkel Mortensen.

Backroom: chief scout Andreas Koefoed and scout René Henriksen join for nothing.

Result: 2–3 to B.93, a league above. Out-shot 22–11 and had 35% of the ball, but Oliver Elliott Karlsen equalised straight after their opener, and Gustav Frederiksen pulled one back in the 95th minute. A respectable start.

First signing: trialist Bastian Andersen, 20, on a free amateur deal. He's 6'3", jumps well (15) and is rated a 5-star prospect. The big man may already be in the building.

story.label: Week 21 · 14–20 November
story.title: Week 21: Robbed, then pegged back
story.body:
The last game before the winter break, away at Hørsholm-Usserød.

Sundby had a goal ruled out on 32 minutes. The match report said it should have stood. Belmaillah made up for it in first-half stoppage time with a solo run and a finish from 20 metres, set up by Becker (7.2). The drought was over.

Then, on 59 minutes, Al-Hummadi crossed from their right, Vandal's side, and Hvid headed in from close range. Vandal lost both his tackles. Another goal from a cross into the middle of the box. Sundby had more shots (8 to 4) and more on target (5 to 2), but Hørsholm-Usserød had the better chances.

To make it worse, Vandal, who played most of the game at left-back, went off injured and Damsgaard replaced him.

Sundby drop to 4th on 24 points, two clear of 7th. The league breaks until 6 March, when Holstebro visit.

Three days later, on 17 November, trialist Hakim Sighaoui signed. The 22-year-old midfielder has the best decision-making in the squad's midfield (14) and 4-star potential. He arrives as cover and competition for Frederiksen.

story.label: Week 22 · 21–27 November
story.title: Week 22: A full-back for the wing
story.body:
Sundby signed 22-year-old Adam Ejler Hansen as a regular starter. He's a left-footed full-back by trade, but Bassett wants him on the left wing.

There's logic to it. In a low block the wingers have to defend, and Hansen can: marking 10, concentration 13, aggression 14. Going forward he brings pace (12), crossing (12) and passing (11). He's rated 3.5 stars now, with 4.5-star potential, the highest ceiling in the squad.

The question marks are his finishing (5) and determination (3).

Off the pitch, Bassett earned his first coaching badge on 27 November, a National C Licence. The staff pushed him into it.

story.label: Week 23 · 28 November–4 December
story.title: Week 23: Top marks, mixed mood
story.body:
Karoli was sold in late November. The board and the fans were both disappointed, but he lost the ball more than anyone in the squad.

The monthly reviews were glowing all the same. The board gave Bassett an A+: "an unbelievable job, clearly the right manager." The fans are ecstatic to be in the promotion race. The small print: tactics only a C+, with complaints that the wing play isn't entertaining, and a reminder that relegation would cost him his job.

The dressing room is calmer. Atmosphere and team cohesion are both only average. Noah Jakobsen was promised more starts and wants them. He, Nybro and Schak are all unhappy that their agreed playing time has changed.

story.label: Week 25 · 12–18 December
story.title: Week 25: Thisted come calling
story.body:
Five months into his first job, Bassett applied for the vacancy at Thisted FC, a club with a national reputation in the CampoBet 2. Division, a league above Sundby.

On 18 December they invited him to interview. The board were "extremely impressed" with his work at Sundby, but have "strong reservations" about his lack of experience keeping teams away from relegation.

story.label: Week 26 · 19–25 December
story.title: Week 26: A Christmas knock-back
story.body:
On Christmas Day, Thisted FC turned Bassett down. Their board liked his plans but decided he wasn't the right person to take the club forward, and appointed Hans Henrik Andreasen instead.

Given that Thisted are bottom of the 2. Division, it may be a lucky escape. Bassett stays at Sundby, 4th and in the promotion race. A few days later the Sundby board announced a cash injection.

story.label: Week 4 · 23–29 January
story.title: Week 4: Halse and Koertz arrive
story.body:
Sundby signed free agent Nicklas Halse after a trial. The 29-year-old is rated 4 stars as a defensive midfielder, the best player in the squad on paper.

He's the ball-winner the side has lacked: tackling 10, anticipation 12, positioning 10, aggression and bravery 14. He brings leadership (13), determination (15) and 221 games of experience, most recently at 2. Division leaders FC Roskilde.

He'll sit in front of the back four, with Becker alongside him to pass. His passing (9) and pace (9) are the limits.

The right wing was fixed too. Oliver Koertz arrived from promotion rivals Næsby: quick, skilful and already the creator of 5 assists in this league. Signing him also weakens a team Sundby are competing with.

story.label: Week 6 · 6–12 February
story.title: Week 6: A left-back who stays at home
story.body:
With Vandal still injured, Sundby signed 32-year-old free agent Nicolai Johannessen to play left-back.

He's a defender first: tackling 11, marking 10, heading 10, concentration 10, and 6'1" to deal with the back-post crosses that have cost Sundby all season. He won't get forward (crossing 7) and he's slow (pace 8), but with full-back-turned-winger Hansen ahead of him, he doesn't need to.

story.label: Week 7 · 13–19 February
story.title: Week 7: Rusty in the wind
story.body:
The first game back after three months off was a friendly at Espergærde, in a strong wind. Bassett picked his new-look first XI: Johannessen at left-back, Halse and Becker in midfield, Koertz on the right. It was a disappointment.

Espergærde had 20 shots to 13, 10 on target to Sundby's 3, and three clear chances to none. Poulsen (7.2) kept it goalless until the 70th minute, when Folkmann Andersen scored. Three minutes later Jovanovski turned the ball into his own net.

Belmaillah (7.1) pulled one back immediately, set up by Trkulja, but it finished 2–1. Becker, Johannessen and Mølvadgaard all struggled. Halse was the best outfield player on his debut (6.9).

story.label: Week 8–9 · 20 February–5 March
story.title: Weeks 8–9: Pre-season wobbles
story.body:
Two more friendlies to finish pre-season. A 1–0 win over Silkeborg II brought a clean sheet. Andersen scored and rated 8.3, and Jørgensen was excellent (7.6).

Then came a scrappy 2–2 with Hellerup, who dominated. Andersen and Pyne-Cole scored, but Sundby managed only 0.44 xG. Langhorn (7.6) was the standout.

Pre-season ended with a record of W1 D1 L1. The worry: Koertz and Halse haven't yet looked like the upgrades they should be, and the attack still isn't creating enough.

story.label: Week 10 · 6–12 March
story.title: Week 10: Déjà vu in stoppage time
story.body:
The league resumed at home to Holstebro, in front of 74 fans on a crisp afternoon. Koertz made his competitive debut.

Christoffer Maul put Holstebro ahead with a fierce shot after six minutes. Andersen equalised four minutes into the second half with a volley into the top corner. Sundby had the better of it, with 11 shots to 6 and xG of 1.47 to 0.90.

Then, in the 92nd minute, Casper Gandrup won it. It was the second time in three league games Sundby had lost to a stoppage-time goal. Bassett admitted he put the wrong sub on up front.

Sundby stay 4th on 24 points, level with ASA. Five games remain in the preliminary phase, and only two points separate 4th from 8th.

story.label: Week 11 · 13–19 March
story.title: Week 11: Pyne-Cole sinks Ishøj
story.body:
Bassett tried his new midfield pairing for the visit of 3rd-placed Ishøj: Frederiksen and Halse, both sitting deep. Ishøj had 60% of the ball and 16 shots to 7, but Sundby made the clear chances, three to none, with xG of 1.69 to 0.76.

Pyne-Cole made the difference. On 73 minutes he finished off a fine team move, set up by Mølvadgaard. In stoppage time he scored again. Maretti's reply came too late.

The win lifts Sundby to 3rd on 27 points, a point above Ishøj. Frem have already qualified for the promotion stage. With four preliminary games left, Sundby are three points clear of 6th.

story.label: Week 12 · 20–26 March
story.title: Week 12: Set-piece meltdown, almost a comeback
story.body:
Away at 11th-placed Vanløse, it fell apart before half-time. A penalty on 33 minutes, a goal from a set piece on 43, and another in first-half stoppage time: 3–0 down, all three from dead balls.

Bassett's half-time talk was blunt ("What was that?! Get your acts together") and the players responded. Andersen came on and scored twice in six minutes, on 72 and 78, both set up by Pyne-Cole (8.5). Sundby pushed for the equaliser but it never came.

The 3–2 defeat drops Sundby to 5th on 27 points, still in the top six but only a point above Ishøj in 6th. Three preliminary games remain.

story.label: Week 13 · 25 March
story.title: Week 13: Outplayed, but Becker rescues a point
story.body:
Away at 3rd-placed ASA, Aarhus, Bassett reshuffled the defence: Jørgensen out, Johannessen into the middle, and Vandal back from injury at left-back.

ASA dominated: 20 shots to 9, 10 on target, xG of 3.74 to 1.23. Poulsen (7.4) and Jovanovski (7.4) held them off until Matos scored on 58 minutes.

Then, for once, a stoppage-time goal went Sundby's way. Becker, playing as a defensive midfielder, timed his run perfectly to finish Pyne-Cole's pass in the 92nd minute. 1–1.

Sundby stay 5th on 28 points, a point above Ishøj. Two preliminary games remain: Brønshøj, then FC Helsingør.

story.label: Week 13 · 29 March
story.title: Week 13: Seven
story.body:
The worst day of Bassett's career. In a downpour at Kløvermarken, 11th-placed Brønshøj scored with almost everything. Olsen after six minutes. A Vandal error let Fæster head in on 12. Olsen again on 17, Fæster's volley on 26: 4–0 inside half an hour.

Belmaillah pulled one back, but Fæster headed his hat-trick goal from point-blank range on 44: 1–5. The half-time message was blunt ("You're letting yourselves down"). Poulsen was taken off, and Harksen made his debut. Noer added a 22-metre volley and Olsen completed his own hat-trick on 63.

It finished 7–1, with two hat-tricks. Fæster was rated a perfect 10. Brønshøj had eight shots on target and seven went in, from an xG of just 2.41.

Sundby drop to 6th on 28 points, one above Vanløse and Holstebro, and the goal difference has gone from +4 to –2. The final preliminary game is away at 2nd-placed FC Helsingør.

story.label: Week 14 · 30 March–5 April
story.title: Week 14: A new deal, despite the seven
story.body:
The day after the 7–1, the board offered Bassett a new contract anyway, and he signed. It runs until June 2028 on the same £3.4K a year, still part-time.

The interesting part is the clauses: a 15% pay rise if Sundby are promoted, and a 35% cut if they're relegated. The board still rate him A+ and the fans are ecstatic.

Bassett also found a likely cause of the recent collapse: the back four was swapping places between the in-possession and out-of-possession shapes. Vandal had been playing centre-back with the ball, which left the defence out of position for crosses. Fixed in time for the last game.

Next: FC Helsingør away, the last game of the preliminary phase, with a top-six place on the line.

story.label: Week 15 · 5 April
story.title: Week 15: What. A. Result.
story.body:
Final day, 7th in the table, one week after the 7–1. Sundby had to go to 2nd-placed FC Helsingør, who'd beaten them in October without facing a shot on target, and win.

With the back four finally lined up properly, Bassett picked Jørgensen and Sørensen in the middle and Halse at right-back. It still started badly: Winkel scored on 20 minutes. Then Jørgensen, dropped a fortnight earlier, equalised on 39 from Mølvadgaard's delivery. On 56 minutes Koertz set up Belmaillah, and Sundby led.

Poulsen, taken off a week earlier, was outstanding (7.6) as Helsingør pushed for an equaliser. It never came. 2–1.

Næsby could only draw with Holbæk, so Sundby crept in: 5th on 31 points, a point above Ishøj. Into the promotion group, where points carry over: Frem 44, ASA and Hørsholm-Usserød 35, Helsingør 33, Sundby 31, Ishøj 30. The top two go up, and 2nd place is four points away with ten games left. The club predicted to be relegated are now playing for promotion.

story.label: Week 16 · 10 April
story.title: Week 16: Promotion group opens with a narrow loss
story.body:
The first promotion-group game was back at ASA, Aarhus, scene of Becker's late equaliser a fortnight earlier. This time there was no rescue.

It was a scrappy, low-key game in the drizzle, broken up by ASA fouls. Viggers' powerful finish from close range on 54 minutes was the only goal. Sundby had just 37% of the ball and few clear openings, though the xG (0.74 to 0.96) shows how little was in it.

At least the defence looked normal again: one goal against, no set-piece disasters. Ishøj visit next.

story.label: Week 17 · 17 April
story.title: Week 17: The bench wins it
story.body:
In the sunshine at Kløvermarken, Sundby played their most complete game in weeks against Ishøj. Andersen finished Belmaillah's pass on 31 minutes. Ishøj equalised through Escobar Jensen on 68.

Then the bench took over. Elliott Karlsen came on and set up Pyne-Cole's header on 82, then Mølvadgaard's goal in stoppage time against his old club. Elliott Karlsen was named player of the match (8.4). Jovanovski (7.5) was outstanding at the back.

Sundby out-created Ishøj (xG 2.50 to 1.69), and the new back four looked settled. Sundby are 5th on 34 points, five behind ASA and Hørsholm-Usserød in 2nd and 3rd, with seven games left. Damsgaard left on a free transfer. Next: Frem.

story.label: Week 18 · 24 April
story.title: Week 18: Frem beaten
story.body:
Frem arrived at Kløvermarken top of the league, already as good as champions. They left beaten.

On 28 minutes Adam Ejler Hansen, the full-back Bassett converted into a left winger, scored his first goal for the club. Then Sundby defended. Frem had 60% of the ball and 10 shots, but only one on target. Langhorn (7.5), Hansen (7.4), Poulsen and Jovanovski (both 7.3) led the way.

The win lifts Sundby to 4th on 37 points, five behind ASA and Hørsholm-Usserød in 2nd and 3rd. Six games left.

story.label: Week 19 · 1 May
story.title: Week 19: Poulsen holds firm
story.body:
Back at Helsingør, scene of the final-day win four weeks earlier. Helsingør had sacked René Skovdahl in the meantime.

On a wet afternoon it finished 0–0. Helsingør had two-thirds of the ball and seven shots on target, but Poulsen saved all of them and was named player of the match (8.1). Sundby had the two clear-cut chances and the better xG (1.77 to 0.84), but couldn't finish them.

The point keeps Sundby 4th with five games left. Hørsholm-Usserød, one of the two sides they're chasing, are next.

story.label: Week 20 · 8 May
story.title: Week 20: Stalemate with the team in 2nd
story.body:
Second-placed Hørsholm-Usserød came to Kløvermarken knowing a win would all but end Sundby's promotion hopes. They left with a point.

It was a tight, cagey game with no clear-cut chances for either side. Hørsholm had 60% of the ball and 11 shots, but only 0.98 xG. The back four held firm again, with Jovanovski (7.2), Langhorn, Jørgensen (both 7.1) and Poulsen (7.0) all solid. Going forward, Sundby managed only 0.25 xG all game, even after Bassett brought on Sighaoui, Koertz, Mølvadgaard and Belmaillah.

That's four games in a row now with one goal or fewer conceded. But Sundby are 4th on 39 points, seven behind Hørsholm and six behind ASA, with four games left. Promotion now needs a miracle.

story.label: Week 21 · 15 May
story.title: Week 21: Mølvadgaard comes home
story.body:
Away at Ishøj, Marcus Mølvadgaard's old club. He scored on 14 minutes from Pyne-Cole's pass. Escobar Jensen equalised on 22, but Mølvadgaard struck again on 29, set up by Elliott Karlsen (7.3).

For once Sundby protected a lead. They created five clear-cut chances to Ishøj's one (xG 2.28 to 1.06), and Jørgensen (7.3) and Jovanovski (7.1) kept it tight for the last hour. 2–1.

Sundby are 4th on 42 points, five behind Hørsholm-Usserød and four behind ASA, with three games left. It's still a long shot, but it's not over.

story.label: Week 22 · 22 May
story.title: Week 22: The lead that held
story.body:
A must-win game at home to ASA, Aarhus, who'd taken four points off Sundby already this season. Mølvadgaard scored after eight minutes, finishing Pyne-Cole's pass, his third goal in two games.

Then came the long wait. ASA had 56% of the ball and 15 shots. With 13 minutes left Bassett switched to Cautious, brought Sighaoui on as a second holding midfielder alongside Frederiksen, and sent Andersen on to defend set pieces. This time the lead held. Jovanovski was immense (8.0) despite being on a yellow, and Poulsen (7.2) made six saves.

Frem and Hørsholm-Usserød drew 2–2. Sundby are 4th on 45 points: one behind ASA, three behind Hørsholm in 2nd, with three games to go. Promotion is back on.

The same day, Thisted FC, the club that turned Bassett down at Christmas, were relegated from the 2. Division.

story.label: Week 23 · 29 May
story.title: Week 23: Frem's party
story.body:
Away at Frem, the league leaders, in a gale at Valby Stadion. Sundby needed a win to stay in the promotion race.

Frem were 1–0 up at half-time and well on top, with six shots on target to Sundby's one. Kretzschmar went on to score a hat-trick, at 26, 53 and 58 minutes, and Almosawe set up all three. He was rated 9.9.

Bassett went for it. Belmaillah came off the bench and set up Andersen for a goal at 72 minutes, but Remmer made it 4–1 in stoppage time. Frem had 69% of the ball and 11 shots on target. No Sundby player rated above 6.8.

After the final whistle, Frem lifted the 3. Division trophy on their own pitch while Sundby watched. Helsingør are next.

story.label: Week 24 · 5 June
story.title: Week 24: Belmaillah's double
story.body:
A week after the defeat at Frem, Bassett changed his front two. Andersen and Belmaillah started up top, with Graini on the left wing.

It worked. Belmaillah scored straight after half-time from Poulsen's long ball, then added a second at 71 minutes from Andersen's pass. He was rated 8.4. At the back, Jovanovski (8.1) and Jørgensen (7.6) kept Helsingør to an xG of 0.49, and Poulsen (7.9) kept a clean sheet.

ASA, Aarhus won too and moved up to 2nd on 50 points. Hørsholm-Usserød are 3rd on 49, with Sundby 4th on 48: two points off 2nd place.

story.label: Week 25 · 12 June
story.title: Week 25: Promoted
story.body:
The final day. Sundby went to Hørsholm-Usserød, who were 2nd, knowing only a win would do, while ASA, Aarhus played bottom side Ishøj.

For most of the game it looked like it would slip away. Hørsholm had 62% of the ball and 10 shots, and by 70 minutes Sundby had managed one shot, with an xG of 0.02. Ishøj were beating ASA, but a draw was no use to anyone in red and white.

Bassett went to Attacking, used all five substitutes, and moved Sighaoui from holding midfield into the centre. At 83 minutes Graini found him and Sighaoui placed a shot into the net. It was Sundby's only shot on target all afternoon, and it won him Player of the Match (7.8). Then came the wait: ASA equalised at Ishøj, but a draw wasn't enough for them. Sundby held on behind two holding midfielders.

There were 179 people at Hørsholm Idrætspark to see it. Sundby finished 2nd on 51 points, one ahead of Hørsholm-Usserød and two ahead of ASA. Champions Frem finished on 60.

Sundby are promoted to the CampoBet 2. Division. Sundby only scraped into the promotion group on the final day of the regular season. Once there, they won six of their ten games. In his first season as a manager, Dave Bassett has won promotion.

The board called the promotion 'unbelievable', and Jørgensen praised Bassett in the press. Prize money for the promotion stage came to £28.7K. The one bit of bad news: Becker picked up an injury.

story.label: Week 26 · 14–16 June
story.title: Week 26: Awards, records and new arrivals
story.body:
The season review put the promotion in context. The board's target for the season was simply to avoid relegation. Sundby finished 2nd and went up. In the Danish Cup they reached the fourth round, which met the aim of being competitive.

The club's awards night at Kløvermarken belonged to Simeon Jovanovski. The 20-year-old centre-back won Fans' Player of the Season, Young Player of the Season and Signing of the Season, averaging 7.03.

The other awards:
• Top scorer: Belmaillah, 12 goals. He also had the best pass completion in the squad (88%).
• Most assists: Pyne-Cole, 8.
• Most Player of the Match awards: Mølvadgaard, 4.
• Goal of the Season: Graini, away at ASA, Aarhus in October.

The Team of the Season, in a 4-4-2: Poulsen; Langhorn, Jovanovski, Jørgensen, Johannessen; Elliott Karlsen, Becker, Frederiksen, Trkulja; Mølvadgaard, Pyne-Cole.

The board's end-of-season review gave Bassett an A-. They called themselves delighted with his leadership, and they especially liked the passing in the Wing Play style. Their criticisms were the 0–0 at home to Hørsholm-Usserød, the 4–1 defeat at Frem, and the sale of Noah Jakobsen. The board also approved a place on the next coaching course.

The record book was busy. Belmaillah broke the club goalscoring record, Mølvadgaard set a new record for Player of the Match awards, Poulsen set a clean-sheet record, and Pyne-Cole set one of his own.

The transfer window opened, and four of the young players from the April trials signed on free transfers: midfielder Noah Kjer, forward Teo Reeh, full-back Magnus Dalager and centre-back Lau Overgaard. All are 18. Jørgensen has been asked to help Reeh settle in.

The 2. Division brings ground rules too. The board announced a £55K expansion of Kløvermarken, adding standing room for 500 more supporters to meet league requirements. A £28K council grant covers about half of it. The work will take around six months, and capacity drops from 1,080 while a stand is closed.

The final numbers for the squad that finished the season: Poulsen played every minute (3,208). Belmaillah scored 12 goals from an xG of 9.9, beating his chances. Mølvadgaard scored 9 from 7.3, Andersen 7 from 6.2 and Pyne-Cole 7 from 6.8. Jovanovski won 6 headers per 90 minutes and the ball back 17 times per 90, the most in the squad. Becker completed 46 passes per 90 at 85%. The four strikers scored 35 of the 40 goals from this squad.

story.label: Week 28 · 10 July
story.title: Week 28: Staying put
story.body:
Promotion made Bassett's name, and he tested the market. He applied for several jobs over the summer, hoping a bigger club would offer a better contract. Every application was turned down.

So it's another season at Sundby, now in the 2. Division. Pre-season is under way, and the trial process has turned up two highly rated teenage wingers, Gabriel Santos and David Manata, along with Ishøj goalkeeper Marius Kruse.

The first summer signing went through: left-back Hüseyin Tümtürk, 21, joined on a free from relegated Holbæk on £9.25K a year until 2028. That's more than double what his manager earns. To make room, two left-backs left the club: Magnus Vandal and the 33-year-old Nicolai Johannessen.

story.label: Week 30 · 31 July
story.title: Week 30: Pre-season done
story.body:
Four pre-season friendlies: a 1–0 defeat at Espergærde, a 3–1 win at Ringsted, a 1–0 home win over Hobro and a goalless draw with Fredericia KFUM. Two wins, a draw and a defeat, with only two goals conceded.

Life in the 2. Division starts with a reunion. The first game is away at Frem, the champions who went up with Sundby, at Valby Stadion, where Sundby lost 4–1 in May. Then come a Danish Cup first-round trip to Hillerød and a home league game against Næstved.

The summer rebuild was done by opening day. Arriving: right-back Rasmus Steuch, centre-back Oliver Wettergren, wingers Khalid Al-Ali, David Manata, Gabriel Santos and Asger Stengaard, and Jonas Buch Dahl, alongside Tümtürk and the four teenagers from the spring trials.

story.label: Week 31 · 31 July
story.title: Week 31: Unlucky at Valby
story.body:
The 2. Division opener, away at Frem. Knaack put the champions ahead after six minutes, but Sundby hit back quickly. Halse finished Al-Ali's pass to make it 1–1 after 18 minutes.

It was far closer than May's 4–1 at the same ground. Frem had 61% of the ball, but the expected goals were almost level (0.79 to 0.75), and Sundby made the only two clear-cut chances of the game. The difference came after 64 minutes, when Frem broke behind the Sundby defence and Wass scored from Simonsen's pass.

Halse (7.3) was Sundby's best player. Sundby's crossing was poor: only 2% of crosses found a teammate.

story.label: Week 32 · 4 August
story.title: Week 32: Out in extra time
story.body:
The Danish Cup first round, away at Hillerød. Andersen put Sundby ahead in first-half stoppage time, set up by new striker Jonas Buch Dahl (7.3).

Sundby were three minutes from the next round. Then, in the third minute of added time, Kretzschmar equalised. It was the same Kretzschmar who scored a hat-trick for Frem against Sundby in May. In extra time, Høyer headed the winner after 107 minutes.

It was close throughout: Sundby had more shots on target (9 to 7) and more clear chances (3 to 2), and the xG was 1.83 to 2.05. Poulsen (7.4) was busy. The worry is a second late goal conceded in two games.

story.label: Week 33 · 7 August
story.title: Week 33: First win in the 2. Division
story.body:
Næstved finished third in the 2. Division last season. They came to Kløvermarken and had 73% of the ball, but Sundby won 3–1.

Khalid Al-Ali needed three minutes to make his mark. He pounced on a mistake by Mads Bager and his shot went in off the woodwork. Full-back Jonathan Krath equalised for Næstved after 39 minutes, but Bastian Andersen headed Sundby back in front on the hour. Simeon Jovanovski sealed it with another header two minutes from time.

Al-Ali was Player of the Match (8.1) on his home debut. Gabriel Santos, 17, made his professional debut. The crowd was 208.

months.title: Pre-season: new boss, blank faces
months.summary:
Dave Bassett arrived at a club tipped to finish 11th of 12, with no transfer budget. The squad met his first team talk with blank faces, and the press conference drew one journalist.

He went bargain hunting: thirteen trialist strikers, seven sent home on day one. Bastian Andersen, Andreas Nybro and Simeon Jovanovski signed, the last taking the entire wage budget. Five more players were released.

The friendlies were mixed: a narrow defeat to B.93, a route-one winner at Roskilde, then a 5–3 hammering by Hellerup. The league opener against Næsby ended in a 2–1 defeat.

months.title: Bottom half, then the turnaround
months.summary:
A 4–0 cup win and a Belmaillah hat-trick at Ringsted promised much. Then came defeats to Vanløse and Frem, and Sundby sank to 10th, looking every bit the relegation favourites.

The Data Hub's verdict was brutal: "very easy to roll over". Bassett tore up the 4-2-4, switched to a cautious low-block 4-4-2, brought in a new back four and released vice-captain Lundqvist.

It worked at once. Mølvadgaard's 112th-minute free kick won the cup tie at Tårnby, and Holbæk were beaten 3–0. Two clean sheets in two.

months.title: Giant-killers and title contenders
months.summary:
Krogh Hansen complained about not starting and was released the same day. Nobody else complained.

Sundby won at third-placed Ishøj, beat league leaders Hørsholm-Usserød, and knocked Superliga AC Horsens out of the cup with another Mølvadgaard winner off the bench. A rotated side lost at Holstebro, but a 2–0 win at second-placed Brønshøj put Sundby back up to 2nd.

Four wins from five, and four clean sheets.

months.title: Stalling at the top
months.summary:
Juel-Berg complained about his broken promise and was released before kick-off against ASA, the fourth senior player let go. Sundby won that one 2–1.

Then the goals dried up. The top-of-the-table clash with FC Helsingør was lost to a free kick, with Sundby managing one shot all game. A goalless draw at Næsby followed.

Mølvadgaard ended the drought against bottom side Ringsted with his sixth goal of the season. Sundby are 3rd, three points off the top.

The cup run ended in the fourth round with a 2–0 defeat to FC Fredericia, a noble exit after three wins and a Superliga scalp.

months.title: Winter comes early
months.summary:
Three games without a win before the break. A tired 1–1 with Holbæk after the cup exit, then heartbreak at leaders Frem, lost in stoppage time after a Kunnerup error.

At Hørsholm-Usserød, Belmaillah ended his drought, but another headed goal from a cross cost two points, and Vandal was injured.

Sundby go into the winter break 4th on 24 points, seven behind Frem and two clear of 7th. Midfielder Hakim Sighaoui signed after a trial, and full-back Adam Ejler Hansen arrived to play on the left wing.

months.title: December
months.summary: The winter break. The board gave Bassett an A+ for November, calling it an unbelievable job, and the fans are ecstatic. Squad harmony is only average, with Jakobsen, Nybro and Schak all unhappy about playing time.

months.title: January
months.summary: The transfer window opened, and Bassett landed his two best signings yet: holding midfielder Nicklas Halse and right winger Oliver Koertz, taken from rivals Næsby.

months.title: February
months.summary: Final preparations for the restart. Left-back Nicolai Johannessen joined. Three friendlies brought a win, a draw and a defeat. Andersen scored in two of them, but the new signings were slow to settle.

months.title: Stoppage time and set pieces
months.summary: The league resumed with a stoppage-time home defeat to Holstebro. A week later, two Pyne-Cole goals beat Ishøj and lifted Sundby to 3rd. Then a set-piece collapse at Vanløse: 3–0 down at half-time, Andersen's late double wasn't quite enough. At ASA, Becker's stoppage-time equaliser rescued a point Sundby barely deserved. Then the low point: a 7–1 home thrashing by Brønshøj.

months.title: Into the promotion group
months.summary: A new contract for Bassett, then the most important win of his career: 2–1 at FC Helsingør on the final day, to finish 5th and reach the promotion group. In the promotion group, a narrow loss at ASA was followed by wins over Ishøj (3–1) and leaders Frem (1–0).

months.title: May
months.summary: The run-in. Goalless draws at Helsingør and at home to Hørsholm-Usserød, then back-to-back wins: Mølvadgaard's double at Ishøj, and his winner against ASA, Aarhus. Then a 4–1 defeat at Frem, who lifted the title on their own pitch.

months.title: Promoted
months.summary: Belmaillah scored twice to beat Helsingør 2–0. Then came the final day at Hørsholm-Usserød. With seven minutes left, Sighaoui scored the only goal, and Sundby finished 2nd. They are promoted to the 2. Division. Jovanovski swept the club awards.

months.title: July
months.summary: Every job application was turned down, so Bassett stays at Sundby for life in the 2. Division.

months.title: August
months.summary: Out of the Danish Cup in extra time at Hillerød, then a first 2. Division win: 3–1 over Næstved.
